methods.label: Bisect the isosceles triangle and check the endpoint
methods.explanation:
The wording needs a qualification. For a fixed triangle with angle \(\theta\), there is no largest real number below \(\theta\): whenever \(t<\theta\), the number \((t+\theta)/2\) is larger than \(t\) and still below \(\theta\).

Assume instead that the question asks for the largest bound that the angle exceeds in every admissible triangle. Write \(AB=c\), \(CA=CB=\sqrt3\), and \(\theta=\angle ACB\). The triangle inequality requires \(3<c<2\sqrt3\).

Let \(M\) be the midpoint of \(AB\). In an isosceles triangle, \(CM\) is both an altitude and an angle bisector. The right triangle \(CMA\) therefore gives
\[
\sin\frac{\theta}{2}
=\frac{c/2}{\sqrt3}
>\frac{3}{2\sqrt3}
=\frac{\sqrt3}{2}
=\sin60^\circ.
\]
Both \(\theta/2\) and \(60^\circ\) are acute, where sine is strictly increasing. Hence \(\theta>120^\circ\).

We must also show that a larger uniform bound cannot work. For any proposed \(t>120^\circ\), choose an angle satisfying
\[
120^\circ<\theta<\min\{t,180^\circ\}.
\]
Construct a triangle with two sides \(\sqrt3\) and included angle \(\theta\). The same right-triangle calculation gives
\[
c=2\sqrt3\sin\frac{\theta}{2}>3.
\]
This is an admissible triangle, but its angle is below \(t\). Thus every larger proposed bound fails. Under the uniform-bound interpretation, \(\boxed{x=120^\circ}\), choice \(\boxed{\text{B}}\); for one fixed triangle, the stated largest real number does not exist.
methods.levelReason: The proof uses an isosceles altitude, acute-angle sine ratios, the special value at 60 degrees, and an explicit geometric construction to establish sharpness.

needsNewNodes.name: Sharp geometric bounds and excluded endpoints
needsNewNodes.description: For a real quantity varying over specified geometric configurations, prove a uniform bound and establish sharpness by producing admissible values arbitrarily close to its boundary. Distinguish an attained extremum, an excluded endpoint, and a bound asserted only for one fixed configuration.
